    StartersVilleneuve market breadToasted baguette with brie and apple, or goat's cheese and honeyHow to make it1 baguette2 tbsp olive oil150g brie2 red apples150g goat's cheese2 tbsp honeySlice the baguette and brush with oil.Toast until golden.Slice the apples thinly.Top half with brie and apple, the rest with goat's cheese and a drizzle of honey.Gaston's tavern devilled eggsBoiled eggs with a Dijon, mayo and chive yolk filling, dusted with paprikaHow to make it12 eggs1/2 cup mayonnaise1 tbsp Dijon mustard2 tbsp chives, snipped1 tsp smoked paprikaBoil the eggs until hard.Cool and peel.Halve the eggs and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, Dijon and chives until smooth.Pipe back into the whites.Dust with smoked paprika and pile onto one big platter.Mrs Potts's coronation chicken sandwichesMrs Potts and Chip serving teaHow to make itAs written, serves 4Crustless finger sandwiches of curried coronation chicken with apricot and almonds, and cucumber with cream cheese, on a tiered stand.Shred 400g roast chicken.Mix 4 tbsp mayo, 2 tbsp Greek yoghurt, 2 tsp mild curry powder, 1 tbsp apricot jam, 40g toasted flaked almonds and chopped coriander, then fold through the chicken.Spread 12 slices of soft bread with butter.Make 4 rounds of coronation chicken and 2 of thin cucumber with 100g cream cheese.Trim the crusts and cut each round into 3 fingers.Pork rillettes with cornichonsGaston eats five dozen eggs. Start smaller.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsLumière's beef and mushroom braiseBeef chuck braised with bacon, baby onions and mushroomsHow to make it150g bacon, diced1.2kg beef chuck, diced2 tbsp olive oil12 baby onions, peeled300g mushrooms2 tbsp plain flour2 tbsp tomato paste750ml beef stock1 tbsp balsamic vinegar4 sprigs of thyme2 bay leaves1kg potatoes60g butter100ml milk1 crusty loafDice the bacon and beef and peel the baby onions.Brown the bacon in the olive oil, then brown the beef in batches.Add the onions and mushrooms and colour lightly.Stir in the flour and tomato paste, then add the stock, balsamic vinegar, thyme and bay leaves.Cover and simmer until the beef is tender.Peel and boil the potatoes, then mash with butter and warm milk.Serve the braise over the mash with crusty bread.Maurice's leek and thyme chickenBelle's father Maurice heading off to marketHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chicken thighs braised with leeks, thyme, mustard and a splash of cream until tender, with crusty bread to mop up every bit of sauce.Season 1kg chicken thighs and brown skin side down in a little oil for 6 minutes, then turn and remove.Soften 2 sliced leeks in 20g butter, add 2 crushed garlic cloves and thyme, then pour in 300ml chicken stock and 1 tbsp Dijon mustard.Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.Stir in 100ml cream and bubble for 5 minutes.Serve with crusty bread.SweetsEnchanted rose tartSweet pastry case with custard and thin red apple slices in circlesHow to make it2 sheets of sweet shortcrust pastry, thawed500ml thick custard3 red apples1 lemon500ml water, for softening the apples3 tbsp apricot jam1 tbsp water, for the glazeLine a tart tin with the pastry.Blind bake at 180°C until pale gold.Cool the case.Slice the apples paper thin. Squeeze the lemon into the 500 ml of water, soften the slices in it briefly, then drain.Fill the case with custard.Arrange the apple slices in overlapping circles into a rose.Bake at 180°C.Warm the jam with 1 tbsp of water and brush over to glaze.Cool before slicing.DrinksBallroom golden peach punchPeach nectar and orange juice with sliced orange and fresh peachHow to make it750ml chilled peach nectar3 oranges1/2 tsp vanilla extract1 fresh peach750ml chilled sparkling apple juice4 cups iceJuice two oranges and slice the third. Slice the peach.Mix the peach nectar, orange juice and vanilla in a big jug.Add the orange and peach slices and chill.Just before serving, add ice and top with sparkling apple juice. Stir gently and pour into wide glasses.
